habitat: Moist deciduous forests; cultivated in temple gardens and avenues
ecological_importance: Flowers attract numerous bees, butterflies, and nectar-feeding birds. Ripe fruits are consumed by fruit bats, squirrels, and arboreal birds, which act as seed dispersers.
threats: Habitat loss in native evergreen forests
field_identification_notes: Dark green, glossy, elliptic leaves with wavy margins.
Intensely sweet, lingering fragrance from small star-shaped white flowers scattered under the canopy.
Ovoid yellow-orange edible fruits and rough dark grey bark.
ml_relevance: Glossy, dark green, elliptic leaves with characteristic wavy margins and star-shaped floral morphology.

ar_information.quick_identification: Glossy wavy leaves; small, highly fragrant star-shaped white flowers; orange-yellow berries.
ar_information.ecological_importance: Provides nectar for insects and nutritious fruit for bats and birds.
ar_information.conservation_message: Least Concern (LC). Dried flowers retain their sweet scent for months and are traditionally used in potpourri and garlands.

vit_campus_relevance.location: Main campus pathways and administrative lawns
